key_insight: A 23-model benchmark showed that no single self-supervised 3D medical foundation model consistently transfers best across segmentation, classification, and regression tasks, so model choice should be task-specific.
clinical_relevance: For medical AI deployment, this work helps teams shortlist foundation models more efficiently before fine-tuning, potentially reducing compute while improving selection for the target task.
method: Benchmarked 23 self-supervised 3D foundation models on 14 labeled downstream tasks.
Compared fine-tuned performance across segmentation, classification, and regression, then tested transferability estimators.
Introduced InsightRank, which uses frozen-feature statistics and architecture-aware pairwise comparisons to rank models pre-fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Mean Kendall tau-b agreement with fine-tuned rankings was 0.431 for segmentation and 0.352 for classification/regression, and a three-model shortlist cut extraction-plus-training job time by 85.8% across seven segmentation tasks.
watch_item: Transferability estimates were less reliable for image-level classification/regression than for segmentation, so shortlist rankings still need validation on the intended task and modality.
paper_title: Benchmarking Self-Supervised 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models and Transferability Estimation
